2024-06-27 00:05 raylynnknight Created from the form at meta:create_new_dataentry_page

Overview: MT7981 dual core CPU using 2.4GHz and 5GHz WiFi (both AX)
128MB NAND flash with two UBI partitions with identical size
1 multi color LED (red, green, blue, white) connected via GCA230718
openwrt_wiki.Installation: Installation via OEM web interface is currently not supported because D-Link uses encrypted images and the crypto keys are changed when updating the OEM firmware (e.g. to 1.10).
Flash Procedure (OpenWrt 24.10.3 and lat: Set your IP address to 192.168.200.10, subnet mask 255.255.255.0
Press the reset button while powering on the device
Keep the reset button pressed until the LED blinks red
Open a Chromium based browser and go to http://192.168.200.1/ (recovery web interface); non-chromium based browsers won't work
The recovery web interface always reports successful flashing, even if it fails
After flashing, the recovery web interface will try to forward the browser to 192.168.0.1 (can be ignored)
Main LED would either stay red or white
OpenWRT initramfs should start in failsafe mode and be accessible at 192.168.1.1
transfer squashfs-sysupgrade.bin over SCP (or LuCI) and flash it
openwrt_wiki.Flash Procedure (24.10.2 and earlier, de: recovery flashes to the currently active partition; OpenWrt in second partition does not boot (LED stays red); fix via UBI switch image https://github.com/RolandoMagico/openwrt/releases/tag/M30-Recovery-UBI-Switch
openwrt_wiki.Active partition: If the devices are shipped, the OEM firmware is running in the first partition (might change in future).
openwrt_wiki.TFTP: Open the case, connect to the UART console; IP 192.168.200.2/24 on a LAN port; tftp server provides openwrt-mediatek-filogic-dlink_aquila-pro-ai-m30-a1-initramfs-kernel.bin; U-Boot menu '7. Load image', '0 - TFTP client (Default)'; initramfs at 192.168.1.1, then sysupgrade
openwrt_wiki.Serial boot (Y-Modem): The default serial baudrate (115200 bps) is also the maximum, so loading an initramfs over UART takes approx 10 minutes
Flash Layout: mtd6 0x06980000 0x00040000 Odm (MAC address and keys for firmware crypto)
openwrt_wiki.Reverting to OEM firmware: possible by flashing a decrypted OEM firmware image via recovery web interface; do not flash images with version < 1.10 if >= 1.10 was already used; keys in Odm partition (firmware key offset 0xDA len 0x2C; public key offset 0x10D len 0x25C (<1.10) bzw. 0x42C (>=1.10))
openwrt_wiki.Failsafe mode: If your device reverts to failsafe after every reboot, you're likely booting of ubi1: fw_setenv bootpart 0
openwrt_wiki.Power: The D-Link AQUILA PRO AI M30 A1 requires a 12V power supply (rated at 1A minimum). The connector is a centre-positive (conventional polarity) 3.5 mm x 1.35 mm barrel jack. 5.5 mm x 2.1 mm female to 3.5 mm x 1.35 mm adapters are available for use with more common 5.5x2.1 adapters. The PCB footprint of the power connector is the same as many commonly available 5.5x2.1 PCB mount sockets if you prefer to swap-out the connector entirely.
openwrt_wiki.Opening the case: There are four screws at the bottom: 2 under the rubber feets, 2 under the label. After removing the screws, the white plastic part can be shifted out of the blue part. Be careful because the antennas are mounted on the side and the top of the white part.
openwrt_wiki.Serial: The serial interface can be connected to the 4 pin holes on the side of the board. Pins (from front to rear): 3.3V, RX, TX, GND. Serial connection parameters: 115200, 8N1, 3.3V
openwrt_wiki.Photos: Vorlage, keine Fotos von Gehäuse, Typenschild, Platine oder Seriell-Anschluss
OEM bootlog (Auszug): SPI_NAND Detected ID 0xc2, Page size 2048, Block size 131072, size 134217728
Macronix SPI NAND was found, 128 MiB
U-Boot Boot Menu: 1. Startup system, 2. Upgrade firmware, 3. Upgrade ATF BL2, 4. Upgrade ATF FIP, 5. Http Upgrade, 6. Upgrade single image, 7. Load image, 0. U-Boot console
OpenWrt bootlog (Auszug): eth0: fixed/2500base-x link mode (CPU-Port zum Switch)
internet: PHY [mdio-bus:00] driver [MediaTek MT7981 PHY], Link is Up - 1Gbps/Full

openwrt_commit.titel: filogic: Add support for D-Link AQUILA PRO AI M30
Specification: MT7981 dual core CPU using 2.4GHz and 5GHz WiFi (both AX)
128MB NAND flash with two UBI partitions with identical size
1 multi color LED (red, green, blue, white) connected via GCA230718
Disassembly: There are four screws at the bottom: 2 under the rubber feets, 2 under the label.
After removing the screws, the white plastic part can be shifted out of the blue part.
Be careful because the antennas are mounted on the side and the top of the white part.
Serial Interface: The serial interface can be connected to the 4 pin holes on the side of the board.
Pins (from front to rear): 3.3V, RX, TX, GND
MAC addresses: WAN MAC is stored in partition "Odm" at offset 0x81
LAN (as printed on the device) is WAN MAC + 1
WLAN MAC (2.4 GHz) is WAN MAC + 2
openwrt_commit.Flashing via Recovery Web Interface: IP 192.168.200.10/24, reset while powering on until LED blinks red, Chromium http://192.168.200.1, recovery.bin; recovery always flashes to the currently active partition, OpenWrt only boots from the first
openwrt_commit.Flashing via U-Boot: UART, IP 192.168.200.2/24, tftp initramfs-kernel.bin, U-Boot menu '7. Load image', then sysupgrade
openwrt_commit.Flashing via OEM web interface: not possible, as it will change the active partition and OpenWrt is only running on the first UBI partition
openwrt_commit.Controlling the LEDs: GCA230718 via I2C (address 0x40), eigener Treiber leds-gca230718
openwrt_commit.Comparison to M32/R32: Entschlüsselung wie M30/M32/R32, nur andere Schlüssel; Recovery-Header mit Prüfsumme über den Datenbereich
openwrt_commit.02_network: dlink,aquila-pro-ai-m30-a1) ucidef_set_interfaces_lan_wan "lan1 lan2 lan3 lan4" internet

DTS.gmac1: label internet, phy-mode gmii, interne GbE-PHY, MAC = Odm-Basis

gluon_pr3816.titel: mediatek-filogic: remove recovery image for D-Link AQUILA PRO AI M30+M60 A1
gluon_pr3816.inhalt: Berichte bei FFMUC und FFRN (https://forum.ffrn.de/t/d-link-m30-flashen-geht-nicht/3645), dass das Gluon-Recovery-Image des M30 A1 nicht installiert; FFAC hatte es schon aus dem Selector genommen; richtiger Weg: OpenWrt-Recovery-Image, dann Gluon-sysupgrade

Schritte: M30 und Computer mit einem LAN-Kabel verbinden
Resetknopf auf der Rückseite mit Büroklammer drücken und gleichzeitig anschalten/einstecken, halten bis die Haupt-LED rot blinkt
http://192.168.200.1/ öffnen, OpenWrt Recovery Firmware hochladen
danach PC wieder auf DHCP; OpenWrt unter 192.168.1.1, dort Freifunk-Sysupgrade-Firmware installieren

werkstatt.Ablauf: RAMpe 20261015 recovery.bin (52428880 B) per curl an die Recovery; LED rot blinkend -> rot dauernd (schreibt) -> weiß schnell -> weiß 1 Hz; RAMpe-Config unter /cgi-bin/config; Gluon-sysupgrade hochgeladen; ca. 5 min von Recovery bis Gluon im Mesh
werkstatt.MAC: Hostname dceae73152d2, MAC dc:ea:e7:31:52:d2 richtig (Odm-MAC dieses Einzelgeräts bei 0x81)
werkstatt.Ergebnis: Anleitung d-link-aquila-pro-ai-m30-a1 mit RAMpe 20261015 komplett durchlaufen: funktioniert; Gluon v2025.1.3-5-g0ad3ad5+, 26100702bro, nef-21_dias

dlink-flashen.md: M30: OpenWrt-Recovery-Image, dann Gluon sysupgrade -n; Gluon liefert bewusst kein Recovery-Image (Gluon #3816, bei uns devices/remove-dlink-m30-recovery)
MAC: M30 aus Mehrfach-Packs (M30/CP) haben den MAC-Eintrag der Werksdaten bei 0x87 statt 0x81; eigener Parser seit gluon-patches-hardware 9901905

Am Einzelgerät bestätigt (01.10.2026): sysupgrade -n von 2023.2 auf 2025.1, MAC-Eintrag bei 0x81, Basis dc:ea:e7:31:52:d1; nach 110 s wieder online; Hardware-MACs: internet …:d1 (Basis), eth0/lan1-3 …:d2, phy0 …:d3, phy1 …:d4
Bestätigung auf 2023.2 (17.09.2026, 26091619bro): beide Bänder mit Client- und Mesh-Interface, Portzuordnung WAN/LAN stimmt, primäre MAC passt zum Aufkleber; MemTotal 499 MB, Overlay 29,7 MB
Preise (adorfer, 01.10.2026): Mehrfach-Pack rund 180 €, einzelner M30 rund 40 €
